incidents.victim: Higher education sector (100+ orgs, incl. University of Nottingham)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) allowing unauthenticated remote code execution and server takeover.
incidents.impact: The ShinyHunters crew claims to have hit 100+ organizations (68% higher education); University of Nottingham confirmed theft of ~455,000 records including passport, financial and protected-characteristic data. Oracle has issued mitigations but no patch; extortion is ongoing.

incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of a max-severity OS command injection flaw (CVE-2026-10520, CVSS 10) in Ivanti Sentry within 24 hours of disclosure, using a public proof-of-concept for unauthenticated root-level RCE.
incidents.impact: Shadowserver observed widespread exploitation attempts and at least two backdoored instances; attackers appeared to have pre-mapped Ivanti assets and struck immediately, risking theft of credentials and lateral movement from the mobile gateway.

incidents.victim: US businesses, educational institutions and other organizations
incidents.vector: Use of stolen session tokens to bypass re-authentication, routed through commercial proxies/VPNs, to harvest bulk email, files and Microsoft Teams content from compromised cloud environments.
incidents.impact: US prosecutors charged Russian national Denis Obrezko for facilitating a large-scale Russia-aligned espionage campaign; the FBI verified intrusions at 11 US companies, described as likely a fraction of the true victim count across NATO states.

incidents.vector: Breach of a government agency managing healthcare entitlements; method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers allegedly stole personal information on more than 67 million Thai citizens, with portions offered on online black markets. The Thai government has launched an investigation.

incidents.vector: Breach traced to a software engineer (a Chinese national who has since left the country) with internal access to customer data.
incidents.impact: A 2025 breach exposed the personal information of 34 million customers; South Korea's privacy regulator fined Coupang $409M (1.7% of annual sales). The company plans to appeal.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the Signal messaging account of a US Representative; the FBI notified the lawmaker of the breach.
incidents.impact: Suspected Russian hackers breached the Signal account of Rep. Don Bacon, a vocal Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic, raising concerns over targeting of US officials' encrypted communications.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupting operational systems at two sugar mills; nature of the attack not confirmed.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer paused cane haulage and milling at the start of the annual crushing season, causing operational disruption.

incidents.victim: US federal civilian agencies (Windows / Microsoft Defender)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a Microsoft Defender elevation-of-privilege flaw (CVE-2026-41091, on CISA's KEV list) plus public PoC exploits from researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' targeting Windows zero-days, including a BitLocker bypass.
incidents.impact: Microsoft's record 206-CVE Patch Tuesday included one actively exploited Defender bug granting full system control and a 'wormable' kernel RCE (CVE-2026-45657, CVSS 9.8); Nightmare Eclipse threatens further exploit releases on July 14.

incidents.victim: Current and former US security clearance holders
incidents.vector: Fake 'consulting company' websites with AI-generated personas and photos posted on hiring platforms to lure clearance holders into selling insider information, paid via crypto from overseas accounts.
incidents.impact: The DOJ and FBI seized 13 internet domains used by suspected Chinese intelligence to recruit current and former US government/military employees with access to classified information; takeover pages now disrupt the scheme.

incidents.victim: Conti ransomware victims (1,000+ orgs incl. Tennessee government)
incidents.vector: Conti ransomware used to encrypt and extort more than 1,000 victims globally between 2020 and 2022, including malware developed by the defendant.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty to Conti-related wire fraud (up to 20 years); the group extorted over $150M, including ~$634K from Tennessee victims and the compromise of a sheriff's department, EMS and police.

incidents.vector: Malicious VS Code 'Nx Console' extension (compromised in the TanStack supply-chain attack) installed by an employee, leading to exfiltration of internal source code repositories.
incidents.impact: More than 3,800 internal GitHub repositories were stolen and offered for sale on a hacking forum; GitHub is rotating critical secret tokens. Grafana traced its own breach to the same TanStack incident.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the university's CareerConnect recruitment platform at the end of May 2026.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole data on alumni, research staff and employers from the platform used to connect students and staff with recruiters about internships and jobs.

incidents.vector: Hijacking of legitimate BlueSky accounts (since April) to post pro-Kremlin and anti-Ukraine propaganda, attributed to the Russian influence group Matryoshka.
incidents.impact: Compromised accounts were used to spread Russian disinformation; BlueSky has been suspending affected accounts until owners could resecure them.

incidents.vector: Breach and defacement of the news outlet's website, deleting articles and disrupting broadcasts.
incidents.impact: Iranian hackers (the Handala group) attacked the independent women's news agency, deleted content, disrupted online broadcasts, and threatened to dox and harm employees.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing operation luring select WhatsApp users to click malicious links leading to an external site, in violation of a US court injunction.
incidents.impact: Meta says it found and disrupted a new NSO Group campaign and filed to hold the sanctioned Israeli spyware maker in contempt, urging lawmakers to keep NSO on the US sanctions list.

incidents.victim: US law firms and professional/financial services
incidents.vector: Voice phishing (vishing) impersonating IT helpdesk to trick staff into screen-sharing and installing remote monitoring tools (AnyDesk, Zoho Assist); in some cases actors entered offices in person to copy data via USB.
incidents.impact: Mandiant tracked UNC3753 ('Luna Moth'/'Silent Ransom') stealing legal agreements, PII and financial records from dozens of US firms, often within a single business day, followed by aggressive three-day extortion demands. The FBI separately warned law firms.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS / GlobalProtect customers
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0257, added to CISA KEV May 29) allowing attackers to circumvent controls and initiate VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed an unidentified actor probing and establishing VPN sessions on vulnerable gateways; no post-access lateral movement seen yet, but only a portion of probed devices connected. Patching and hunting urged.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a Red Hat employee GitHub account to push malicious orphan commits, triggering CI/CD pipelines to publish 32 Trojanized npm packages ('Miasma') with valid SLSA provenance, bypassing code review.
incidents.impact: The 'Mini Shai-Hulud' style worm harvested GitHub/npm tokens, SSH keys, and AWS/GCP/Azure and Kubernetes credentials across ~80,000 weekly downloads, extending the post-Shai-Hulud wave of self-propagating npm supply-chain attacks.
